ActiveRiskPayload.description:
How tracking error against a benchmark divides among active positions.

Contributions sum to `tracking_error` exactly, the same identity the total
decomposition satisfies — on active weights rather than holdings.

contributions_not_held.description: Contributions from benchmark constituents the index does not hold. They have no row in the weights table but are often the largest active positions there are, so omitting them would hide the biggest sources of tracking error.
contributions_not_held.title: Contributions Not Held

covered_weight.description: Share of *gross* active weight the model covers. Gross because active weights sum to roughly zero, so a plain sum would say nothing about coverage.
covered_weight.title: Covered Weight

tracking_error.description: Annualised volatility of the active position.
tracking_error.title: Tracking Error

uncovered.description: Names with no estimate, from either side.
uncovered.title: Uncovered

ActiveRiskPayload.title: ActiveRiskPayload

raw_weight_history.description: The same dates -> the weight before capping. Added alongside `weight_history` rather than replacing it, so the drilldown can show what the cap did to this name over time without breaking a client reading only the applied series.
raw_weight_history.title: Raw Weight History

weight_history.description: Rebalance date -> this name's applied weight. Only the rebalances it was actually in.
weight_history.title: Weight History

AttributionView.description:
Response of `GET /beacon/{index_id}/attribution`.

Contributions are Carino-linked, so they sum to the compounded total return
rather than approximately to it. `residual` is reported regardless and
should sit at machine epsilon; anything larger means an assumption broke
upstream, which is worth surfacing rather than rounding away.

cap_drag.description: Capped return minus uncapped. Null on an uncapped index: reporting 0.0 would claim capping happened and made no difference.
cap_drag.title: Cap Drag

cost_drag.description: Direct effect of transaction costs. Null at zero cost.
cost_drag.title: Cost Drag

AttributionView.title: AttributionView

BacktestMetrics.description:
Headline metrics from a backtest run.

Tracking figures are null when the run had no target index to compare to.
BacktestMetrics.title: BacktestMetrics

benchmark.description: Optional external benchmark. The tracked index is always reported separately; this adds a second comparison.

start.description: Start date, YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to the index base date.
start.title: Start

transaction_cost_bps.description: Cost per trade in basis points of notional.
transaction_cost_bps.title: Transaction Cost Bps

BatchReferenceResponse.description:
Response of `GET /data/reference`.

Entries are in the order the request named them, one per identifier, so a
table can render straight down the list without re-sorting against what it
asked for.

as_of.description: Point-in-time date applied, if one was requested.
as_of.title: As Of

BatchReferenceResponse.title: BatchReferenceResponse

BenchmarkRef.description:
What to compare a backtest against.

Distinct from the index being tracked. The tracked index measures
replication accuracy; a benchmark measures relative performance against
something the portfolio was never trying to replicate.

kind.description: 'index' for a stored index definition, 'identifier' for a market-data series.
kind.title: Kind

price_column.description: Market-data column to read. Ignored when kind is 'index'.
price_column.title: Price Column

BenchmarkRef.title: BenchmarkRef

CarryDecomposition.description:
Carry split into the pieces a person can reason about.

Each part is the price effect of one rate acting alone. They do not sum to
the total exactly, because carry compounds rather than adds; the residual
is reported rather than spread across the parts, which would make each of
them slightly wrong in order to hide that the split is approximate.

residual.description: Total minus the three parts — the compounding the decomposition cannot attribute.
residual.title: Residual

CarryDecomposition.title: CarryDecomposition

CompareEntry.description: One index within a comparison, on the shared window.

level.description: Rebased to 100 on the first shared date, so lines start together and the comparison is of shape, not scale.

CompareEntry.title: CompareEntry

observations.description: Dates every index covers. Fewer than any one of them carries alone whenever their spans differ.
observations.title: Observations

ConcentrationPayload.description: How concentrated a weight vector is.

effective_assets.description: 1/HHI: how many equally weighted names would be as concentrated. Lower than the raw count whenever weights are uneven.
effective_assets.title: Effective Assets

top_weights.description: Combined weight of the largest N, keyed by N.
top_weights.title: Top Weights

ConcentrationPayload.title: ConcentrationPayload

ConstituentRow.description:
One constituent's row in the weights table.

Everything a row needs is here, so the table renders from one response
rather than joining three. The two weights are the point: `raw_weight` is
what the weighting scheme produced, `weight` is what survived the cap, and
the difference is what capping moved.

active_risk_contribution.description: This name's share of tracking error. **Can be negative**: an underweight that hedges an overweight genuinely reduces tracking error, and hiding that behind an absolute value would misreport what the index is doing.
active_risk_contribution.title: Active Risk Contribution

active_weight.description: Weight minus the benchmark's, when a `benchmark` was given. Negative is an underweight.
active_weight.title: Active Weight

capped.description: Whether this name was held at the cap on this rebalance.
capped.title: Capped

delta_since_rebalance.description: Held weight minus target weight, for this name, as of `as_of`. Null when `as_of` is the rebalance date itself: the weights were just set, so nothing has drifted and a zero would claim a measurement rather than its absence.
delta_since_rebalance.title: Delta Since Rebalance

raw_weight.description: Weight before capping. Equal to `weight` on an uncapped index, and the only way to see what the cap cost.
raw_weight.title: Raw Weight

risk_contribution.description: This name's share of the index's annualised volatility, in the same units. Populated only when `risk=true` was requested; null also when the risk model has no estimate for this constituent, which `risk.uncovered` lists.
risk_contribution.title: Risk Contribution

shares_outstanding.description: The company's shares outstanding on this date, from market data. Deliberately NOT the number of shares the index holds — that is a different figure needing a divisor and a notional, and naming this one `shares` would let the two be confused silently.
shares_outstanding.title: Shares Outstanding

ConstituentRow.title: ConstituentRow

ConstraintRow.description:
One constraint, in the shape a client's editor holds it.

Maps 1:1 to a class in `beacon.optimise.constraints`: the row a user edits,
the JSON that is stored and the object the solver receives are the same
thing in three representations, so a rule cannot change meaning in
translation.

id.description: Stable row id. Carried back on any binding constraint so a client can highlight the row that bound.
id.title: Id

params.description: Constructor arguments for that class, by name.
params.title: Params

ConstraintRow.title: ConstraintRow

id.description: Stable identifier, used in the URL.
id.title: Id

ConstraintTypes.description:
Response of `GET /optimise/constraint-types`.

Served so a client builds its editor from the same source the solver reads,
rather than from a copy that drifts.

specs.description: The same constraint types in the richer shape `/indices/rule-types` uses, so one client component can render both editors.
specs.title: Specs

types.description: Constraint type -> the parameters it accepts. Kept for clients written against the original shape; `specs` carries the same set with everything needed to render it.
types.title: Types

ConstraintTypes.title: ConstraintTypes

ContributionPayload.description: One constituent's share of the index return.
ContributionPayload.title: ContributionPayload

CorporateAction.description:
One corporate action.

`kind` is the authoritative answer to what `value` means, and the reason a
client needs no list of type strings. Reading `type` and inferring cash or
ratio from a hardcoded list works until a type the client has never seen
arrives, at which point it renders as whichever the list defaults to —
confidently, and wrongly.

kind.description: What `value` means. 'cash' is an amount per share and adds up; 'ratio' is a share-count multiplier and compounds; 'structural' (rights issue, spin-off, merger) carries no directly aggregable value and should not be rendered as a quantity in either column.
kind.title: Kind

pay_date.description: Payment date, ISO 8601, where the source knows it. Null means unknown — omit the field in the UI rather than dashing it, since a dash reads as 'there is none'.
pay_date.title: Pay Date

status.description: Lifecycle state, where the source knows it. Null means unknown, not 'not yet announced'.
status.title: Status

type.description: Action type, e.g. DIVIDEND or SPLIT. A closed set the engine validates on load, but branch on `kind` rather than on this: new types are added, and a client that matches type strings breaks silently when one is.
type.title: Type

value.description: Cash amount per share for cash actions; a share-count multiplier for ratio actions. What it means depends on `kind`, so the two are never summed together.
value.title: Value

CorporateAction.title: CorporateAction

CorporateActionsResponse.description:
Response of `GET /data/corporate-actions/{identifier}`.

Carries the raw history and the two aggregates that need the whole series
to compute, so a client asking "what did this pay" does not have to
reimplement the trailing window and get its boundary subtly wrong.

cumulative_split_ratio.description: Compounded share-count multiplier across the returned window. 1.0 when there were no splits.
cumulative_split_ratio.title: Cumulative Split Ratio

trailing_dividend.description: Ordinary dividends per share over the twelve calendar months ending at the as-of date.
trailing_dividend.title: Trailing Dividend

trailing_dividend_yield.description: Trailing dividend over the close on the as-of date. Null when no price is available — a missing price is a reason to say nothing rather than to guess.
trailing_dividend_yield.title: Trailing Dividend Yield

CorporateActionsResponse.title: CorporateActionsResponse

cache_size_bytes.description: Total bytes on disk for the whole store. Null when no store backs this process.
cache_size_bytes.title: Cache Size Bytes

identifiers_union.description: Distinct identifiers across every dataset. Not the sum of the per-dataset counts: a name present in both market and reference data would otherwise be counted twice, and 'assets covered' would exceed the universe.
identifiers_union.title: Identifiers Union

DataSourceStatus.description: Whether this process has a data source, and how much it covers.

configured.description: True when a DataFetcher is attached.
configured.title: Configured

DataSourceStatus.title: DataSourceStatus

DatasetCoverage.description: What the loaded data actually spans, for one dataset.

cache_age.description: Seconds since this dataset was last loaded or synced. Null when the dataset is not loaded at all, which is a different statement from 'loaded and never refreshed'.
cache_age.title: Cache Age

cache_size_bytes.description: Bytes the backing store occupies on disk. Null when the data did not come from a store, in which case it has no size to report rather than a size of zero.
cache_size_bytes.title: Cache Size Bytes

field_count.description: Data columns this dataset holds, excluding the identifier and date keys.
field_count.title: Field Count

frequency.description: How often this dataset is expected to change: 'daily', 'static' or 'event'. The engine's definition of what stale means, so a client renders staleness from this rather than from thresholds of its own.
frequency.title: Frequency

last_refreshed.description: When this dataset was last loaded or synced, ISO 8601. Carried alongside the age because an age is only meaningful at the instant it was read, and a client holding a response for a minute needs the timestamp.
last_refreshed.title: Last Refreshed

source.description: Where the data was loaded from, e.g. 'synthetic', 'yfinance', 'local'. Null when a fetcher was assembled in-process and nothing recorded a provenance.
source.title: Source

stale_after_seconds.description: Age beyond which this dataset should read as stale. Published so the mapping from frequency to a duration lives in one place; null means the question does not apply, as for static data.
stale_after_seconds.title: Stale After Seconds

DatasetCoverage.title: DatasetCoverage

DriftPayload.description: How far weights moved between two rebalances.

turnover.description: Half the total: the one-way trading needed to return to target, since every overweight funds an underweight.
turnover.title: Turnover

DriftPayload.title: DriftPayload

ErrorDetail.description: The body of an error envelope.

code.description: Stable machine-readable code; safe to branch on.
code.title: Code

detail.description: Structured context, e.g. the offending field or rule.
detail.title: Detail

ErrorDetail.title: ErrorDetail

ErrorEnvelope.description: Every non-2xx response uses this shape.
ErrorEnvelope.title: ErrorEnvelope

ExposuresView.description:
Response of `GET /optimise/runs/{run_id}/exposures`.

Factors are the ones derivable from price and share count — size, momentum,
volatility — plus a market intercept. Value and quality are absent rather
than approximated: a momentum factor built from prices is the real thing, a
value factor faked without book values would not be.

r_squared.description: Read against a floor of roughly k/n rather than against zero: fitting k factors to an n-asset cross-section explains about that much by construction.
r_squared.title: R Squared

ExposuresView.title: ExposuresView

Finding.description: One validation result, addressable to the rule that caused it.

path.description: Dotted path to the offending field.
path.title: Path

rule_id.description: Id of the rule responsible, when there is one.
rule_id.title: Rule Id

Finding.title: Finding

FrontierPoint.description: One portfolio on the efficient frontier.
FrontierPoint.title: FrontierPoint

expected_returns.description: Annualised historical mean returns, per name. A poor forecast, and the honest one: it is the only return estimate derivable from the data the server holds. A caller with a real view should supply it.
expected_returns.title: Expected Returns

monotonic.description: Whether risk rises with return across the grid. Always true for a correct solve, so a false here means a point did not reach optimality.
monotonic.title: Monotonic

FuturesPriceRequest.description:
Body of `POST /derivatives/futures/price`.

Stateless: every input the calculation needs is here, and nothing is read
from or written to storage.

curve.description: Zero-rate pillars as {tenor_in_years: rate}. A flat curve and a scalar rate give identical answers, so supplying one changes nothing unless the curve has shape.
curve.title: Curve

dividends.description: Discrete cash dividends as (years_to_ex, amount). When present these are used instead of the continuous yield: the two are different models of the same thing and applying both would double-count.
dividends.title: Dividends

grid_tenors.description: Rows of the sensitivity grid, in years.
grid_tenors.title: Grid Tenors

market_price.description: Quoted price, for the basis and implied repo. Both are null without one rather than computed against the theoretical value, which would make them identically zero.
market_price.title: Market Price

risk_free_rate.description: Continuously compounded financing rate. Ignored when `curve` is supplied.
risk_free_rate.title: Risk Free Rate

time_to_expiry.description: Years to expiry. Dates win when both are given, being the less ambiguous statement.
time_to_expiry.title: Time To Expiry

FuturesPriceRequest.title: FuturesPriceRequest

contract_value.description: Fair value times multiplier times contracts.
contract_value.title: Contract Value

financing_rate.description: Rate used, read off the curve.
financing_rate.title: Financing Rate

implied_repo.description: Financing rate the quoted price implies, when quoted.
implied_repo.title: Implied Repo

sensitivity.description: Fair value across a tenor x rate grid, centred on this contract.

cache_age.description: Seconds since the market data was last loaded or synced. Null only when no data source is configured — there is then nothing whose age could be reported.
cache_age.title: Cache Age

base_value.description: Index level on the base date.
base_value.title: Base Value

calendar.description: Exchange MIC backing trading-day arithmetic, e.g. 'XNYS'. Null means Monday to Friday, which is what every index defined before this field used. Naming one requires the `calendars` extra — an index that declares a calendar must never quietly compute against a different one.
calendar.title: Calendar

effective_lag_sessions.description: Sessions between a rebalance being announced and its weights taking effect. Stored now, honoured by the calculator in BN-126; until then it is declared and not applied, and 0 is the behaviour in force.
effective_lag_sessions.title: Effective Lag Sessions

id.description: Stable identifier, used in the URL.
id.title: Id

publication_time.description: When the level is published, e.g. '18:00 America/New_York'. Display metadata: it says when a figure is released and changes no figure, so nothing in the calculation reads it.
publication_time.title: Publication Time

rebalance_day_rule.description: Which day of a scheduled month the rebalance falls on: FIRST_BUSINESS_DAY, LAST_BUSINESS_DAY or THIRD_FRIDAY. A date landing on a holiday rolls back to the previous session.
rebalance_day_rule.title: Rebalance Day Rule

rebalancing_frequency.description: MONTHLY, QUARTERLY, SEMI-ANNUAL or ANNUAL. The cadence; `rebalance_day_rule` decides which day of the month.
rebalancing_frequency.title: Rebalancing Frequency

return_type.description: How returns accumulate. PRICE ignores distributions; TOTAL_RETURN reinvests them across the index by shrinking the divisor; NET_TOTAL_RETURN does the same after withholding tax. PRICE is the default, so an index defined before this existed is unchanged.
return_type.title: Return Type

withholding_tax_rate.description: Fraction of each distribution withheld, for a net index. A flat index-level rate rather than a per-country table: a table is only as good as the country field behind it, and an unpopulated one produces a number that looks precise and is not. Ignored unless `return_type` is NET_TOTAL_RETURN.
withholding_tax_rate.title: Withholding Tax Rate

error.description: Failure reason, when status is failed.
error.title: Error

result.description: Present only once the job has succeeded; null otherwise.
result.title: Result

status.description: pending, running, succeeded, failed or cancelled. The last three are terminal.
status.title: Status

as_of.description: Which rebalance to target, YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to the latest.
as_of.title: As Of

index_id.description: Index whose weights are the target.
index_id.title: Index Id

risk_free_rate.description: Used for the frontier's tangency point.
risk_free_rate.title: Risk Free Rate

start.description: Start of the window the risk model is estimated over.
start.title: Start

ParameterSpec.description:
One parameter of a configurable type, described well enough to render.

Names, types, defaults and whether a parameter is required are read from
the constructor, so they cannot drift from what the code accepts. Labels,
ordering and choices are declared on the class, because a signature cannot
carry them.

choices.description: The accepted values, when this is a closed set. Null means any value of `type` is allowed.
choices.title: Choices

default.description: Value used when omitted. Null both for 'no default' and for a default of None; `required` distinguishes them.
default.title: Default

help.description: One line of guidance for the field.
help.title: Help

name.description: Parameter name, as it must appear in `params`.
name.title: Name

required.description: Whether the constructor rejects the call without it.
required.title: Required

type.description: Display type: number, integer, boolean, string or json. What control to render, not the Python annotation.
type.title: Type

ParameterSpec.title: ParameterSpec

PipelineSpec.description: The grouped rule pipeline: Selection, Weighting, Treatment.
PipelineSpec.title: PipelineSpec

capped.description: Whether this name sits at the cap.
capped.title: Capped

excluded_at.description: Waterfall position where it dropped out.
excluded_at.title: Excluded At

excluded_by.description: Id of the first rule that excluded it. Null when included.
excluded_by.title: Excluded By

included.description: Whether it reached the final index.
included.title: Included

uncapped_weight.description: Weight before capping, when the cap bound this name.
uncapped_weight.title: Uncapped Weight

weight.description: Final weight as a fraction. Null when excluded.
weight.title: Weight

PreviewDocumentRequest.description:
Body of `POST /indices/preview`, which previews a document as supplied.

The route for a draft. The by-id route reads what is stored, so while an
editor holds unsaved changes its figures describe the old definition — with
nothing on screen to say they are stale. This one previews exactly what was
sent, so editing a rule updates the resolved figures without saving.

as_of.description: Date to evaluate the pipeline at, YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to the document's base date.
as_of.title: As Of

document.description: The definition to derive, saved or not.

PreviewDocumentRequest.title: PreviewDocumentRequest

PreviewRequest.description: Body of `POST /indices/{id}/preview`, which previews the *saved* index.

as_of.description: Date to evaluate the pipeline at, YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to the index's base date.
as_of.title: As Of

PreviewRequest.title: PreviewRequest

cap.description: Cap applied, as a fraction, if any.
cap.title: Cap

cap_redistributed.description: Weight moved off capped names onto the rest.
cap_redistributed.title: Cap Redistributed

total_weight.description: Sum of the final weights; 1.0 for a non-empty index.
total_weight.title: Total Weight

weights.description: Final weights as fractions, keyed by identifier.
weights.title: Weights

PreviewStep.description:
One rung of the derivation waterfall.

There is one of these per selection rule, in pipeline order, plus a first
entry for the universe itself so the funnel starts from a stated total.

excluded.description: Identifiers this step removed. Empty for the universe row.
excluded.title: Excluded

position.description: 0 is the universe; rules follow in order.
position.title: Position

rule_id.description: Rule responsible, or null for the universe row.
rule_id.title: Rule Id

PreviewStep.title: PreviewStep

ReferenceEntry.description: One identifier's row in a batch reference response.

fields.description: Requested reference columns and derived fields. A column the dataset holds but this identifier has no value for is present and null, which is a different statement from the identifier being absent.
fields.title: Fields

found.description: Whether the reference dataset holds this identifier. False leaves `fields` empty rather than failing the batch, so one unknown name does not lose the other 511.
found.title: Found

ReferenceEntry.title: ReferenceEntry

ReferenceResponse.description:
Response of `GET /data/reference/{identifier}`.

Fields are whatever columns the loaded reference data carries — the
library does not impose a schema on it — so they are returned as a
mapping rather than as named attributes.

fields.description: Reference columns for this identifier, e.g. NAME, CURRENCY, EXCHANGE. Timestamps are ISO 8601 strings.
fields.title: Fields

ReferenceResponse.title: ReferenceResponse

index_id.description: Required for a built-in template, which is generated from that index's latest completed backtest. Ignored for a stored template, which is rendered exactly as saved.
index_id.title: Index Id

template_id.description: A stored template, or a built-in such as FACTSHEET-A4.
template_id.title: Template Id

built_in.description: Templates generated from a run rather than stored. These can be rendered but not edited: they are code, not documents.
built_in.title: Built In

ReportTemplateDocument.description:
A stored report template, as JSON.

Blocks are kept as free-form mappings rather than a discriminated union so
the wire shape stays exactly what `beacon.report.blocks` reads and writes.
A second definition of the same thing here is a second definition to keep
in step, and the block model already validates its own rows on the way in.

blocks.description: Content, drawn top to bottom. Each carries a `kind`.
blocks.title: Blocks

template_id.description: Stable identifier, used in the URL.
template_id.title: Template Id

ReportTemplateDocument.title: ReportTemplateDocument

RiskDecomposition.description:
Active risk split into factor and specific parts.

The two sum to the total exactly, because the covariance is *defined* as
``B F Bᵀ + D``. Pair an arbitrary covariance with arbitrary loadings and
there is a cross term; the identity belongs to this model and not to any
pairing of a matrix with some exposures.

contributions.description: Each factor's share of the factor variance. May be negative: a factor position that hedges another genuinely reduces risk.
contributions.title: Contributions

residual.description: Total minus the two parts. Zero up to float noise, by construction.
residual.title: Residual

RiskDecomposition.title: RiskDecomposition

RiskDiagnosticsPayload.description: How an estimate was produced, and how far it can be trusted.

average_correlation.description: Mean off-diagonal correlation. The sanity check a person can actually do: a diversified equity universe sits around 0.3-0.6, and a figure far outside that says the window or the universe is not what someone thought.
average_correlation.title: Average Correlation

condition_number.description: Largest eigenvalue over smallest. An optimiser inverts this matrix, and a large value means the inverse amplifies estimation error rather than reflecting it.
condition_number.title: Condition Number

intensity.description: Weight placed on the structured target. 0 means the estimate is the raw sample covariance.
intensity.title: Intensity

observations.description: Periods used, after dropping incomplete rows.
observations.title: Observations

positive_semi_definite.description: Computed from the eigenvalues, not asserted. A matrix that fails this can produce a negative portfolio variance, and a caller about to invert it needs to know.
positive_semi_definite.title: Positive Semi Definite

RiskDiagnosticsPayload.title: RiskDiagnosticsPayload

identifiers.description: Names to estimate over. Empty uses the index named by `index_id`.
identifiers.title: Identifiers

index_id.description: Take the universe from this index's latest run instead of listing names.
index_id.title: Index Id

intensity.description: Weight on the target, in [0, 1]. Null uses the heuristic from the panel's shape; 0 gives the raw sample covariance, which on a short history across many names is mostly noise.
intensity.title: Intensity

repair.description: Clip negative eigenvalues if the result is not PSD. Off by default because shrinkage should make it unnecessary and clipping silently shifts the variances.
repair.title: Repair

target.description: Structured target to shrink toward: 'constant_correlation' or 'scaled_identity'.
target.title: Target

correlation.description: Symmetric with a unit diagonal, by construction.

volatilities.description: Annualised standard deviation per asset — the square root of the covariance diagonal.
volatilities.title: Volatilities

RiskPayload.description:
How the index's volatility divides among its holdings.

Contributions sum to `volatility` exactly rather than approximately — the
decomposition is an identity, so a client can show the parts and the whole
without them disagreeing.

covered_weight.description: Fraction of the index the figure speaks for. Below 1.0 when the model has no estimate for some constituent; the covered names keep their real weights rather than being renormalised, which would restate the portfolio.
covered_weight.title: Covered Weight

uncovered.description: Constituents with no estimate, usually for want of history. Listed rather than only counted, so a reader sees which names are missing.
uncovered.title: Uncovered

volatility.description: Annualised volatility of the covered holdings, at the weights they are actually held.
volatility.title: Volatility

window_end.description: Last date of the estimation window.
window_end.title: Window End

window_start.description: First date of the estimation window.
window_start.title: Window Start

RiskPayload.title: RiskPayload

RollResponse.description:
Response of `GET /derivatives/{index_id}/roll`.

Both legs are priced theoretically off the same spot and curve, so this is
the *carry* roll rather than a market one.

annualised_roll.description: Positive in backwardation, negative in contango.
annualised_roll.title: Annualised Roll

RuleSpec.description: One rule in the pipeline, addressable by its id.

id.description: Client-assigned id, unique within the pipeline.

Everything a methodology editor needs to render a real form: which rules

selection.description: Eligibility rules available for the selection stage.

weighting.description: Weighting schemes available for the weighting stage.
weighting.title: Weighting

findings.description: Non-blocking warnings. Errors would have prevented the save.

SavedIndex.description: Response of a successful save: the document plus any warnings.

ScheduleView.description:
Response of `GET /indices/{index_id}/schedule`.

Derived, not stored: the next rebalance is a function of the schedule, the
calendar and today, and storing it would leave a date that silently expires.

as_of.description: Date the answer was computed from.
as_of.title: As Of

days_until.description: Calendar days from `as_of` to `next_rebalance`. Calendar days rather than sessions, because it is displayed as 'in 57 days' and a reader counts those on a wall calendar.
days_until.title: Days Until

next_rebalance.description: Next rebalance date, ISO 8601. Null when none falls within the lookahead — which happens only for a schedule this server cannot project, not for a normal index.

recent.description: Rebalances already passed, most recent last.
recent.title: Recent

TreatmentSpec.description: The treatment group of the pipeline.

corporate_actions.description: How corporate actions affect the index. Only ADJUST_DIVISOR is supported.
corporate_actions.title: Corporate Actions

TreatmentSpec.title: TreatmentSpec

rate.description: Reference rate for the period: the fixing for the current one, the curve's forward for later ones.
rate.title: Rate

curve.description: Zero-rate pillars for projecting future periods. The current period always accrues at the rate already fixed at its reset.
curve.title: Curve

futures_prices.description: Prices to compute breakeven spreads against.
futures_prices.title: Futures Prices

initial_price.description: Level at inception or last reset.
initial_price.title: Initial Price

reference_rate_value.description: Its current fixing, as a decimal.
reference_rate_value.title: Reference Rate Value

reset_type.description: UNFUNDED accrues reference + spread; FUNDED accrues only the spread, and therefore has no rate sensitivity at all.
reset_type.title: Reset Type

breakeven.description: Breakeven financing spread against each supplied futures price — what makes a swap and a future agree.
breakeven.title: Breakeven

dv01.description: Value change per +1bp. Negative for a receiver, who pays financing — the sign carries the information a magnitude would lose. Exactly zero on a funded swap, where only the spread accrues.
dv01.title: Dv01

fair_spread_bps.description: Spread at which the trade would be worth nothing today. Null when no time has accrued, where no spread could balance it.
fair_spread_bps.title: Fair Spread Bps

present_value.description: Total return leg minus accrued financing, from the receiver's side.
present_value.title: Present Value

name.description: Class name, as it must appear in `type`.
name.title: Name

summary.description: One line describing what it does.
summary.title: Summary

Where an index's universe comes from.

Either a reference to a stored universe or a literal list. `identifiers`

id.title: Id

WatchlistUpsert.description:
Body of `PUT /data/watchlists/{id}`.

The id comes from the URL, so it is not repeated here — accepting it in
both places invites the two to disagree.

WeightingSpec.description: The weighting group of the pipeline.

max_weight.description: Cap on any single constituent's weight, as a fraction (0.1 is 10%). Applied after the scheme and iterated until nothing breaches it. Null means uncapped.
max_weight.title: Max Weight

WeightingSpec.title: WeightingSpec

active_risk.description: The tracking-error decomposition, when a `benchmark` index was named alongside `risk=true`.

announced_date.description: When that composition was published, if earlier than `rebalance_date`. Null when the index has no lag.
announced_date.title: Announced Date

drift.description: Movement since the previous rebalance. Null at the first, where there is nothing to have drifted from.

rebalance_date.description: Rebalance in force on that date. An index holds the weights set at its last rebalance until the next one, so this is usually earlier than `as_of`.
rebalance_date.title: Rebalance Date

risk.description: The volatility decomposition, when `risk=true` was requested. Null otherwise: estimating a covariance over every constituent is the pane's whole cost, and nobody should pay it without asking.

rows.description: Per-constituent detail, heaviest first. Carries the same applied weights as `weights`, which is kept because charts and concentration maths want a mapping while a table wants ordered rows.
rows.title: Rows
